title.narrative: AKYAS Sanitation

description.narrative: [b]The project aims to adapt and implement a new container-based sanitation system with a sustainable business model among rural households in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh. The system provides safely managed sanitation, on-site fecal sludge management, and upcycling of fecal waste into valuable by-products. We will evaluate the social acceptability of the system and test different business models, and prepare to scale the solution to reach more households. The project’s goals are to improve access to sanitation and upcycle fecal waste in a financially sustainable manner within the local toilet economy[/b]

title.narrative: S1- Total number of current unique users served by the initiative with access to improved and safe sanitation products and services

description.narrative: Fill in total number of unique current users for sanitation. Disaggregated per: Male/Female. Type: Domestic users (private and households), school users and for other public users (e.g markets and hospitals, communal users etc) Finally disaggregate users that are provided with a Safely managed / Basic service / Limited service from the initiative. The initiative must tick all criteria to be considered as that service level. 1) Safely managed service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation service is not shared with other households - the initiative ensures that human excreta are safely disposed in situ or transported and treated off-site 2) Basic service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation facility is not shared with other households - initiative does not ensure that human excreta and urine is safely disposed / transported / treated 3) Limited service: Usually at baseline level, but cannot be included at target level. This includes, open pits, unimproved pit latrines, unlined pits, no slabs, prone to flooding etc \* This is indicative of the reach and scale of the initiative in reaching new users with its products and services in terms of the service level that is being provided (as defined by JMP).

title.narrative: Other indicators (P) and narrative explanation
Please provide a short narrative explanation of the data here. (max 250 words)

actual.value: > The key achievement of the final phase, include the introduction of an effective effluent treatment system alongside the upgraded EDU (flagship product). Rigorous lab tests showed excellent results. > The pace of installing AKYAS sanitation systems in households was accelerated dramatically in parternship with different organisations towards the end, with almost half of all installations done within only 1 month. > We observed the that there is in general a "latent demand", a time gap between demand generation and actual demand activation. > AKYAS participated in renowned global knowledge sharing (and advocacy) activities including presentations at Emergency Environmental Health Forum in Switzerland and UNC Water and Health Forum to reach to a wide audience (in person and on-line). Yet it is not possible to provide an accurate number of our outreach through these events (In-person audience in our sessions are estimated to be at least 80 people). Therefore the number is not recorded in the RsR platform. > By the endline reporting period, we have built our initial presence across 5 districts and 8 unions at a small scale. We observed that one sanitation entrepreneur (SE) can cover a union (~3,000 households). There is a potential for a much larger scale training of sanitation entrepreneurs and masons. By tapping into partner's existing network of entrepreneurs and approaches in reaching bigger scale projects, such as that of iDE, the journey of growth can be accelerated. Our new partnership with iDE goes beyond the the VIA Water Programme period, and we are currently working with them on an installation guide that is intuitive and easy to understand. We anticipate this guide to be a tool for larger scale installation training.

The main achievement during the Inception Phase is the co-creation process that resulted in a strong off-the-shelf product - the EDU - that suits the sanitation entrepreneur business model, as well as to raise awareness of safe faecal sludge management, benefits of liquid-solid separation, as well as the brand image of AKYAS as a reliable sanitation brand that could be trusted.
